text: Explain 3/2 direction control valve with its representation - Q 2) a) Distinguish between sensors and actuators with examples b) Write PLC ladder logic diagram as per the operational sequence given below figure. He li Storage paral * fluid tank of   Run/stop plastic pellets oe valve Heatel bd = |< ae et Solenoid C Ls? LS3 [ Si 6 Closed q _|Open — Ratchet as e . gearhead (4 )~«—— Hydraulic i Stationary {_ Cylinder \ My motor Safety gate dic   : 5 Movable 1 ON   dicnlate i at 1 Plate ~~~ Holding pin —— : : - —~ Solenoid B Solenoid {| B: AF" (Opens die plate) fe (Closes die plate) Ls1i An explanation of the operational sequence follows: The machine consists of a set of die plates, a cylinder, a storage barrel, and a safety gate I/3 cover. The mechanical movements are activated by a hydraulic motor and various solenoids. The purpose of the die plate is to create a mold to form the plastic part into the desired shape. A storage tank with a pre-heater holds plastic pellets. When activated, the pre-heated pellets are gravity fed into the cylinder. The cylinder has two functions. First as the piston rod retracts, it compresses the pellets. The compression action creates heat and transforms the pellets into a liquid state. Next, it injects the molten plastic into the mold after the dies are closed. The cylinder piston is retracted by a powerful spring and is extended by a hydraulic motor that is connected to a rack-and-pinion mechanism. Before the injection process can be performed, a safety gate, which protects the operator from injury, must be in place. Step 1: With limit switch LS1 closed by shifting the gate and pushing the momentary start button, rung 0 becomes True. Step 2: As output B3/0 is energized, rung 1 becomes True and latches. This action activates solenoid A, which causes the die plate to close. Step 3: When the die reaches the fully closed position, it closes limit switch LS3, which causes rung 2 to latch. As output O:2/1 becomes True, it causes Examine-Off contact O:2/1 to make the condition of rung 1 False. With rung 2 True, solenoid B becomes activated and pulls the holding pin out of the notch of the piston rod, allowing the spring to retract the cylinder rod and compress the pellets. Step 4: As output O:2/1 becomes energized, Examine-On contact O:2/1 in rung 3 becomes True and causes timer T4:0 to start. While the timer is counting, the molten plastic is allowed to cool and solidify. Step 5: After 10 seconds, the timer times out, activates the DN output, and puts rung 4 into a True condition. With output O:2/2 energized, solenoid C is activated and starts the hydraulic screw motor, which retracts the piston. Step 6: When the piston becomes fully retracted, it closes limit switch LS4. With Examine- On contacts O:2/2 and I:1/3 True, rung 6 becomes True. By energizing output B3/1, rung 5 becomes latched, the timer in rung 3 resets, and rung 2 becomes False. Solenoid B is de-energized, which causes the holding pin to be reinserted into the notch of the piston rod and rung 6 to latch. Step 7: As output O:2/3 becomes True, solenoid D is activated and the die plate retracts. Contact O:2/3 in rung 7 also becomes True. Step 8: The retraction also causes limit switch LS3 to open, making Examine-On contact I:1/2 of rung 5 False, causing rung 5 to be in a False condition. Step 9: When the die plate is fully retracted, it closes limit switch LS2 and makes rung 7 True. By energizing output B3/2 rung 6 becomes unlatched. Step 10: The gate is opened by a machine operator, and the part is removed. The next cycle begins when the gate is closed and the push button is pressed.
